clue.text: Dessert Pooter's ordered? He knows a thing or two

definitions.text: He knows a thing or two

parts.note: Mr Pooter is the narrator of The Diary of a Nobody, so Pooter's means belonging to a nobody
a fool is a dessert of puréed fruit and cream

explanation.surface: Someone asks what pudding Pooter ordered, then praises a knowing person.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Pooter is the hero of the Grossmiths' comic novel The Diary of a Nobody, so the dessert Pooter orders is a nobody's fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is no one's dupe is shrewd and worldly, a person who knows a thing or two.

clue.text: Head teachers

definitions.meaning: slang for the head or skull
the National Union of Teachers, a British trade union, abbreviated

explanation.definitionFit: Nut is slang for the head, and NUT is the National Union of Teachers in Britain.

clue.text: Outer room up north, internally mostly badly constructed

indicators.note: says one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: in Scots a but is the outer room of a two-roomed cottage, as in but and ben

indicators.note: the word loses its last letter, leaving most of it

parts.note: ill can mean badly, as in ill-treated

explanation.surface: A Scottish cottage's front room has been shoddily put together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up north' points to Scotland, where a 'but and ben' is a two-roomed cottage, the but being the outer room. ILL shortened by 'mostly' gives IL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something built has been constructed; the two past participles are synonyms.

clue.text: Such obtuseness can be relative

parts.note: stupidity of one kind, and also the physics quantity that can be measured as a relative value against water

explanation.surface: A remark that dimness may be only a matter of comparison.
explanation.walkthrough: Relative density is the ratio of a substance's density to that of water, so 'relative' turns the dullness into physics.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both thickness of mind and mass per unit volume, which can be given as relative density.

clue.text: Exhibiting neatness fashionable in Bristol

parts.note: alludes to the nautical phrase about being tidy and in Bristol fashion

explanation.surface: A remark that tidiness is the trend in Bristol.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying 'shipshape and Bristol fashion' comes from the port of Bristol, a city in south-west England, where ships had to be well secured.
explanation.definitionFit: Shipshape means neat and in good order, half of the idiom shipshape and Bristol fashion.

clue.text: If not well, it may be 4

definitions.text: If not well, it may be 4

parts.words: If not well, it may be 4
parts.note: something linked with oil that is not a well could be a vessel, the first part of the answer at 4

explanation.surface: A puzzle remark about what something becomes if it is not healthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well' is not health but an oil well; an oil tanker, a ship, is the other thing named from oil. 4 is SHIPSHAPE, whose first part is SHIP.
explanation.definitionFit: An oiler is a ship that carries oil, a tanker, rather than a well that produces it.

clue.text: Is prone, possibly, to accept child's understatement

indicators.note: the outer word takes the other inside it

parts.note: someone who is prone lies down, so is prone gives lies
a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: Someone lying flat might take in a youngster's modest remark.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'child's' stands for 'has', not a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Litotes is the figure of speech of understating by denying the opposite, as in not bad.

clue.text: Fairylike being the Spanish originally feared

parts.note: el is the Spanish for the

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Spanish folk once dreaded a creature from fairyland.
explanation.definitionFit: An elf is a small being of folklore with magical powers, a fairy-like creature.

clue.text: Only creature in river free from blame

indicators.note: puts the following pieces inside the river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
one can mean only, as in the one person who knew
a rat is a creature

explanation.surface: A single animal swimming in a river is declared innocent.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe is a river in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: To exonerate is to clear someone of blame, a direct synonym.

clue.text: In which it's on the cards the queen might turn up

definitions.text: In which it's on the cards the queen might turn up

parts.words: In which it's on the cards the queen might turn up
parts.note: describes a card trick where a punter bets on finding the queen among three cards

explanation.surface: A forecast that a royal visit is likely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the cards' means likely, but here it is literal: in three-card monte the punter must pick out the queen.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the three-card trick, also called three-card monte, in which the queen must be spotted.

clue.text: Regularly occurring test involving English inn up

indicators.note: the test wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: a trial is a test

indicators.note: up can mean turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A recurring examination includes English and a pub turned upside down.
explanation.walkthrough: The held text 'in pub' is a scanning slip for 'inn up'; 'up' giving NNI works even in an across clue, since it means turned over.
explanation.definitionFit: Triennial events recur every three years, so they occur at regular intervals.

clue.text: Old Norse character — a prickly type

definitions.meaning: a runic letter used in Old Norse and Old English for the th sound
a spine on a stem, or by extension a person who is a constant irritation

explanation.definitionFit: Thorn names both the rune for the th sound and a sharp spike on a rose.

clue.text: Little man on good terms with head of Secret Service

parts.note: Matt is the short form of the man's name Matthew
to be in with someone is to be on good terms with them

indicators.note: takes the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A small man gets along well with the chief of MI6.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Secret Service' reads as one phrase, but only its first word gives a letter and 'Service' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Mattins, or matins, is the morning prayer service of the Church of England.

clue.text: Force to misrepresent European victory as fantasy

parts.note: to make someone do something is to force them to
to belie is to give a false picture of
VE Day marked Victory in Europe in 1945

explanation.surface: Someone is pressured into lying about a win in Europe, which proves imaginary.
explanation.definitionFit: Make-believe is pretending or imagining, the stuff of fantasy.

clue.text: It may be secluded, but it isn't unbeatable!

definitions.text: It may be secluded, but it isn't unbeatable!

parts.words: It may be secluded, but it isn't unbeatable!
parts.note: a quiet hideaway, and also what a beaten army does

explanation.surface: A quip that a hideout can still be overcome.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half points to a peaceful hideaway; the second to the military sense, falling back when beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: A retreat is both a secluded refuge and a withdrawal by a defeated force.

clue.text: Girl in pool

definitions.meaning: A girl's name, a pet form of Katherine
a shared fund of money, as in a card game

explanation.definitionFit: Kitty is a girl's name and also a pooled fund of stakes or contributions.

clue.text: Which Chinese dynasty used roofing material ?

parts.note: that can stand for which, as in the book that I read
the Ch'ing, or Qing, was the last imperial dynasty of China

explanation.surface: A question about which Chinese dynasty used a certain roofing material.
explanation.definitionFit: Thatching is straw or reed used to cover a roof, a roofing material.

clue.text: American rebel captures vehicle in surprise attack

indicators.note: the outer pair holds the other inside

parts.note: Jack Cade led a rebellion in Kent in 1450
a bus is a vehicle

explanation.surface: An American insurgent seizes a vehicle in an ambush.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack Cade led a revolt against Henry VI in 1450.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambuscade is an old word for an ambush, an attack from hiding.

clue.text: Sculpture soundly identified by stand-in at Nag's Head?

indicators.note: signals that the phrase is said aloud

parts.note: the Nag's Head is a common British pub name, and a stand-in at a pub is the bar's relief

explanation.surface: A sculpture identified by a replacement worker at a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The Nag's Head is a typical name for a British pub; a stand-in barman is the bar's relief, said like the sculptor's term.
explanation.definitionFit: Bas-relief is sculpture in which figures stand out only slightly from the background.

clue.text: Vulgar self-assertion of supporter by quiet loch

parts.note: a bra supports the bust
sh is a call for quiet
Ness is a famous Scottish loch

explanation.surface: Coarse cheek shown by someone backing a quiet Scottish lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Brashness is loud, crude self-assertiveness, an exact synonym.

clue.text: Fairytale character receiving duke's New Year gift

indicators.note: the character takes in the other letter

parts.note: Hansel, brother of Gretel in the Grimm tale
D is an abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A storybook boy accepts a duke's present at New Year.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'duke's' adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A handsel is a gift for luck, traditionally given on the first Monday of the New Year.

clue.text: He's sometimes spotted with Henry's woman

parts.note: Hy. is an old written abbreviation of the name Henry
Ena is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A man is occasionally seen in company with Henry's lady.
explanation.walkthrough: Old records shorten Henry to Hy., as William to Wm. The 'spotted' animal is the spotted carnivore, not a man seen in public.
explanation.definitionFit: The spotted species is the best known of its kind, so this scavenger is sometimes spotted.

clue.text: Unfortunate fellow ' losing head? Not so

indicators.note: drops the first letter of the word

parts.note: a chap is a fellow
less means not so much, to a smaller degree

explanation.surface: A luckless man loses his head, though perhaps not quite.
explanation.definitionFit: Hapless means unlucky, a straight synonym of unfortunate.

clue.text: Brief study in secular environment

indicators.note: puts study inside the word for secular

parts.note: laic means lay, not of the clergy
to con is to study or learn by heart

explanation.surface: A short course of learning in a non-religious setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Environment' repeats the idea of 'in', the secular word surrounding the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Laconic means using very few words, so brief in speech.

clue.text: How to increase, say, this ancient measure of length?

indicators.note: signals that the phrase is spoken

parts.note: one way to make a number much bigger is to raise it to the third power

explanation.surface: A question about how to enlarge an old unit of length.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How to increase' is the instruction 'cube it', which sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cubit is an ancient unit of length based on the forearm, about eighteen inches.

clue.text: No hype put out about university? It sounds good

indicators.note: the anagram goes round the other letter
the letters are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Removing the hype from a university brings a pleasing sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put out' rearranges NO HYPE into EPHONY, and 'about' puts U inside after E.
explanation.definitionFit: Euphony is pleasantness of sound, so it is literally something that sounds good.

clue.text: Live 'in one's first quarters, having generous corporation

indicators.note: puts the verb inside the other letters
takes the opening letter of the word

parts.note: S and E are compass points, quarters of the compass
to be is to live or exist

explanation.surface: Someone lives in their first lodgings and grows a large belly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' is an old jocular word for a paunch, so a generous one means a big belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Being very fat means having a large paunch, which old slang called a corporation.

clue.text: Eastern royal possibly backing Hebrew prophet

indicators.note: the word is read backwards

parts.note: a royal is a small sail above the topgallant, an example of a sail

explanation.surface: An eastern monarch supporting an ancient prophet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Royal' is not a king but a ship's sail high on the mast.
explanation.definitionFit: Elias is the Greek form of Elijah, the Hebrew prophet in the New Testament.

clue.text: Can bishop show proficiency on horseback?

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a good rider can ride well

explanation.surface: Asking whether a bishop can display skill in the saddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' is not the verb but slang for prison; a Bridewell was a London house of correction.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridewell is an old word for a jail, and can is slang for prison.

clue.text: Beat on which US criminals commonly escape?

definitions.text: on which US criminals commonly escape?
definitions.meaning: fugitives are said to be on the run, in American slang on this

explanation.definitionFit: Lam is to beat, and in US slang being on the lam means fleeing the law.

clue.text: Work unit across river, say

indicators.note: the two letters span the other one

parts.note: eg, for example, means say

explanation.surface: A unit of work done on the far bank of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The erg is the unit of work or energy in the centimetre-gram-second system.

clue.text: Release, pent-up feelings, but forgive erring mates

parts.note: to let off is to excuse without punishment

indicators.note: the letters stray from their order

explanation.surface: Someone vents their emotions yet pardons wayward friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erring' rearranges MATES into STEAM.
explanation.definitionFit: To let off steam is to release pent-up feelings, an idiom from steam engines.
